title: Calibrating a Fluorescence Microscope for Microplastic Identification
author: Kukkola, Krause, et al.

steps.title: Screen filter for microplastics
steps.instruction: Screen the filter under fluorescence mode to identify particles with light intensity above 100 a.u.

steps.title: Identify putative microplastics
steps.instruction: Apply the identification keys to any particle with light intensity above 100 a.u. to rule out false positives and identify microplastics.

steps.title: Screen for fibers
steps.instruction: Screen the filter specifically for fibers using bright-field mode and apply the fiber key for assessment.

steps.title: Perform chemical verification via FT-IR
steps.instruction: Analyze a subset (approximately 30%) of identified fibers and fragments using FT-IR spectroscopy.

substeps.instruction: Filter selected particles onto 25 mm silver membranes.
Use a Bruker Hyperion 2000 microscope coupled with a Vertex 70 FT-IR spectrometer.
Acquire spectra using a 20 x Ge-tipped ATR lens.
Assign identities by spectral searching in a Bruker polymers database with a minimum Hit Quality Index of 60%, prioritizing peak position over peak intensity.

steps.title: Perform chemical verification via Raman spectroscopy
steps.instruction: Analyze a subset (approximately 30%) of identified particles using Raman spectroscopy.

substeps.instruction: Transfer particles onto anodiscs (Whatman, 25 mm diameter, 0.2 µm pore size).
Use a Renishaw InVia Qontor Raman microscope equipped with a 785 nm laser.
Set objective to 10x, slit width to 65 µm, 1200 l/mm, spatial resolution < 1 µm, and spectral resolution < 1 cm−1.
Set laser intensity to 10% of the system (approximately 15 mW).
Perform 10 accumulations of 1 s exposures, repeated three times per particle.
Pre-process spectra in Spectragryph v1.2.15.1 using the advanced baseline function (coarseness = 10, offset = 0) and advanced smoothing function (Savitsky-Golay filter, window = 10, order = 3).
Match processed spectra using the Pearson correlation coefficient for the fingerprint region against SLOPP, SLOPP-E, and in-house reference libraries.
